description: What scripts/browser-walk.mjs measured of the rendered page at one capture step, written beside the screenshot as response/artifacts/<capture>.measurements.json and named by the walk-result's capture record (measurementsRef). A capture is not a measurement: the screenshot, the accessibility snapshot and the DOM record carry no computed value, and under @tools/browsercontrol mode playwright the agent may run no browser code, so every number a measurable proof lane judges — a font size, a target's height, a contrast ratio, a gap — is read from this record and nowhere else. The runner computes it in one page-side evaluation of a self-contained function: one entry per element the accessibility tree exposes plus every element carrying an id, a data-contract or a data-testid, in document order, capped at elements.maxItems (elements that carry an id, a data-contract or a data-testid, or expose an interactive, heading, landmark, image, dialog or status role are kept first when the page exceeds the cap). ref is the element's role and accessible name spelled as a walk target is (`<role> "<name>"`, with ` nth=<n>` when the pair repeats), else a stable CSS path from body; contrast is the WCAG ratio of the computed color over the effective background (the nearest non-transparent background up the tree, composited), rounded to two decimals, null when either colour cannot be resolved.

capture.description: The capture step's name; the screenshot of the same name is the frame these numbers describe.

bbox.description: getBoundingClientRect in CSS pixels, rounded to two decimals.

computed.description: getComputedStyle values as the browser resolves them. backgroundColor is the effective one — the element's own when opaque, else the nearest opaque ancestor's, composited through any translucent layer between; the page canvas counts as white.

dataContract.description: The data-contract attribute split on whitespace; present only on an element that carries one.

text.description: The element's rendered text, whitespace collapsed, the first 80 characters.
